note: Every visible text string the homepage served on the day this was recorded. verify-acceptance.mjs asserts each is still a substring of the flattened server HTML. A replacement homepage must carry all of them, or the difference must be a deliberate, recorded copy decision — not a side effect of the build. Re-recorded 2026-08-19 across two waves — co-visibility, then the layout critique. Every difference from the 2026-08-14 recording is an authorized copy decision listed in `changes`, with the reason it was made and, where the sentence still exists somewhere, where it went.
strings: Anaks Labs — websites built for AI search
Your customers ask AI first. Your site should be
Google, and the assistants your customers ask, do not see your website the way you do. They read the code underneath it — and a great deal of what is on your screen never reaches them.
We build your site first. You decide after you've seen it.
Your customers have already started asking AI.
This is not a forecast. It is a survey of 1,002 US adults, published this year, counted below. Every figure on this site is listed with its source on
of US consumers, up from 6% a year earlier
asked AI to recommend a local business.
Seven times as many people in twelve months. What comes back is a shortlist, not a page of blue links.
BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey 2026. 1,002 US adult consumers.
of adults aged 30 to 44 asked AI for a business recommendation in the past year — the highest of any age band, and the one with the money.
of consumers read reviews on Google — down twelve points in a year. Google is not going anywhere, but it is no longer the only room the decision happens in.
the last is about where people read reviews, not about search generally.
Which raises one question, and it is the only one this page is really about:
when an assistant goes to read your website on a customer's behalf, what does it actually get?
It looks finished. It can still be unreadable.
None of this shows up when you look at your own website.
Your most important sentence is a picture

Your best line is set into the page as an image, so the type looks exactly right. A person reads it. Google receives an empty box where that sentence should be, and nothing can quote a sentence it was never given.

The panels that change on their own. Usually they are not in the page when it arrives — a script adds them a moment later. What a visitor swipes through, Google and the assistants are often never handed at all.
Prices, details and instructions posted as downloads. A person can open it. An assistant is far less likely to quote it.
Nothing tells a machine what you actually do

No questions answered in the format search engines recognise, no page for each thing you offer, no opening hours anywhere a machine can pick them up. Organised to a person, one undifferentiated block of text to a machine.
A phone number and a contact form, and no way to tell which visits turned into customers.
We pick an industry, go and audit it properly, and build the offer around what we actually find there.

We build the site, take it live on your domain, and then run it every month: a performance report, eight posts written to be found and quoted, inquiry and booking tracking, and hosting, maintenance and self-serve editing. One plan, everything in it.
There is no second tier to be upsold to. Your exact numbers come with the finished site, before you sign anything.
What that covers, month by month →
Search results and AI answers are ranked lists — if we optimized two competing businesses in the same neighborhood, we would be competing against our own clients.

Anaks Labs is a software company that designs, builds and runs its own products — this is one of them. The people who design your site write the code, publish the posts and send the report. There is no account manager in between.
You won't find a wall of client logos on this page.
The build we send you is the reference
Until we have built yours, here is a specimen we built both sides of →
Paste your address and see what a search engine actually receives from your site. The rebuild offer is at the end of the result.
Free, no signup, a few seconds.

changes.was: None of this shows up when you look at your own website. It shows up when something has to read that page and answer a question with it.
changes.now: None of this shows up when you look at your own website.
changes.why: The section became a two-column sticky pair and the lede is now a caption above a five-row table; the second sentence restated the table.

changes.was: We pick an industry, go and audit it properly, and build the offer around what we actually find there. Clinics is where we have done that work.
changes.now: We pick an industry, go and audit it properly, and build the offer around what we actually find there.
changes.why: The h2 above it says “We build for clinics” and the link below it says “See the clinics page”.

changes.was: Dental practices and clinics. We opened their websites and read what a search engine actually receives — then built the service around what was missing.
changes.why: Went with the card it lived in. Kept, it made the overlay copy 430px tall at 1440 and past 500px at 1100, running down through the junction box into the ribbon, and the scrim that then cleared the contrast gate was .88 — enough to erase one of the three panels the photograph is about. This is the one cut not enumerated in the brief; restoring it means restoring the card or accepting that scrim.

changes.was: We cap how many clients we take in each area. Search results and AI answers are ranked lists — if we optimized two competing businesses in the same neighborhood, we would be competing against our own clients. One business wins, or nobody does.
changes.now: Search results and AI answers are ranked lists — if we optimized two competing businesses in the same neighborhood, we would be competing against our own clients.
changes.why: First sentence restates the h2; last sentence restates the first.

changes.was: There is no countdown here, and no number of seats: the cap is a condition of the work, not an offer that expires.
changes.why: A footnote denying a scarcity device the page no longer contains.

changes.was: Seven times as many people in twelve months. What comes back is a shortlist, not a page of blue links, and being on it is a different job from ranking. How any given assistant assembles that shortlist is not published by the companies that build them, and we do not claim to know. What is not in dispute is the floor: a page that never hands over a sentence cannot have that sentence quoted from it.
changes.now: Seven times as many people in twelve months. What comes back is a shortlist, not a page of blue links.
changes.movedTo: /sources/#ai-local, under a new “What we don’t claim” row
changes.why: The tail is epistemics — the limits of what we know about how assistants rank. It is the right paragraph in the wrong room: it belongs beside the source it qualifies, not inside a sales page's headline figure. Not deleted; moved verbatim but for the clause that gave it its antecedent.

changes.now: One section credit carrying all three anchors: “Source and sample for AI recommendations →, the same by age band →, and reviews read on Google →”
changes.why: Three cards each repeated the survey name and the same link label. The LINKS are the sourcing discipline and all three survive, by name; only the repetition went.
